tier_reason: No numbers anywhere show a speed win: the CMP README only has a 'Fast, Lightweight, Flexible, and Robust' heading with qualitative text. The ludocode/schemaless-benchmarks shootout would meet tier-A methodology (public code src/cmp/cmp-write.c and src/msgpack/msgpack-c-pack.c, GCC 5.3.0, -O3 -flto flags, AMD Phenom II X6 1090T), but it shows CMP v14 slower than msgpack C 1.3.0 on every write row, so it is evidence against the claim, not for it.

corrections.workload: Encoding (write test) of randomly generated schemaless data (2367-byte small and 248571-byte large MessagePack objects) into a growable buffer in the ludocode/schemaless-benchmarks suite, with the hash cost subtracted. CMP's incremental reader is also timed, but msgpack-c has no incremental-parser row in the suite, so only the write test is a like-for-like comparison against the baseline.
corrections.caveats: Not faster than the named baseline. Every write row in the shootout (README and full-results-extended.md) has CMP v14 slower than msgpack C 1.3.0: desktop 7.33 vs 6.42 us small and 660.19 vs 544.24 us large; Raspberry Pi 89.75 vs 69.21 us and 9206.05 vs 8142.64 us; the extended results add an Intel Celeron 2957U Chromebook with 14.01 vs 11.90 us small and 1463.82 vs 1338.33 us large. Both write tests produce the same output hash (1a9c6681 small, b4ac134d large), so the numbers are real. CMP has no tree parser; its incremental reader is faster than msgpack C's tree unpacker on large data (533.46 vs 750.87 us desktop, 5713.58 vs 10287.89 us Raspberry Pi, derived from page data) but slower on small desktop data (7.43 vs 6.47 us), and that is a cross-category comparison, not a like-for-like win. The shootout was written by the author of MPack (a competitor; its own disclaimer says it may be biased), dates from 2016 (GCC 5.3.0, CMP v14, msgpack-c 1.3.0; the MPack README's feature table now lists CMP v19 and msgpack-c v3.3.0), and the CMP write test uses a harness-supplied growable buffer (buffer.h) because CMP has none, which the author notes is unfair for embedded comparisons. CMP's only measured advantage is code size in the desktop speed build (3232 vs 4088 bytes for write); in the Raspberry Pi -Os build msgpack C is smaller (1528 vs 2324 bytes). No numbers anywhere support a speed claim; candidate for the not-faster shortcoming list.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup match the shootout README rows for CMP (v14) and msgpack C (1.3.0); metadata checked on github.com (370 stars, 85 forks, MIT, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2025-08-06, stale). Keep as a documented not-faster entry: shortcoming 'slower than msgpack-c on write in an independent (MPack-author) shootout; no first-party numbers; only wins on desktop code size'. Not a reject because the evidence is valid, just unfavourable.
